questions.q:
A series is given with one term missing. Select the correct alternative from the given ones that will complete the series.

 264, 270, 276, 282, 288, 294, ?, 306
questions.solution:
Each term increases by 6: $264 \to 270 \to 276 \to 282 \to 288 \to 294$. So the missing term is $294 + 6 = 300$, and $300 + 6 = 306$ completes the series.

**Answer: 300**
questions.shortcut: Constant gap of 6 — just add 6 to 294.

questions.q:
A series is given with one term missing. Select the correct alternative from the given ones that will complete the series.

 -39, -82, -168, -340, -684, ? , -2748, -5500
questions.solution:
Each term is obtained by multiplying the previous term by 2 and subtracting 4: $-39 \times 2 - 4 = -82$, $-82 \times 2 - 4 = -168$, $-168 \times 2 - 4 = -340$, $-340 \times 2 - 4 = -684$. Missing term $= -684 \times 2 - 4 = -1372$; check: $-1372 \times 2 - 4 = -2748$ and $-2748 \times 2 - 4 = -5500$ ✓.

**Answer: -1372**
questions.shortcut: Rule: next = (previous × 2) − 4.

questions.q:
A series is given with one term missing. Select the correct alternative from the given ones that will complete the series.

 -72, -218, ?, -1970, -5912, -17738
questions.solution:
Each term is obtained by multiplying the previous term by 3 and subtracting 2: $-72 \times 3 - 2 = -218$, $-218 \times 3 - 2 = -656$. Check: $-656 \times 3 - 2 = -1970$ ✓, $-1970 \times 3 - 2 = -5912$ ✓, $-5912 \times 3 - 2 = -17738$ ✓.

**Answer: -656**
questions.shortcut: Rule: next = (previous × 3) − 2.

questions.q:
A series is given with one term missing. Select the correct alternative from the given ones that will complete the series.

 M, T, A, H, ?, V, C, J
questions.solution:
Each letter moves 7 places forward in the alphabet (wrapping after Z): M → T → A → H → ? → V → C → J. From H (8th letter), $8 + 7 = 15$th letter = O, and O + 7 = V ✓, V + 7 = C ✓, C + 7 = J ✓.

**Answer: O**
questions.shortcut: Add 7 to letter positions cyclically; H(8) + 7 = 15 → O.

questions.q:
A series is given with one term missing. Select the correct alternative from the given ones that will complete the series.

CX, GB, MG, QK, WP, ?, GY, KC
questions.solution:
First letters C → G → M → Q → W → ? → G → K move alternately +4, +6 (cyclically): W(23) + 4 = 27 → A. Second letters X → B → G → K → P → ? → Y → C move alternately +4, +5: P(16) + 4 = 20 = T. Check: A + 6 = G ✓ and T + 5 = Y ✓. Missing cluster = AT.

**Answer: AT**
questions.shortcut: First letters +4/+6, second letters +4/+5 alternately; from WP: 23 + 4 = A, 16 + 4 = T.

questions.q:
A series is given with one term missing. Select the correct alternative from the given ones that will complete the series.

PP, NL, LH, JD, HZ, ?, DR, BN
questions.solution:
First letters decrease by 2 (P → N → L → J → H → F → D → B) and second letters decrease by 4 cyclically (P → L → H → D → Z → V → R → N). After HZ comes F (H − 2) and V (Z − 4 = 22), i.e. FV; the next terms DR and BN fit the same rule ✓.

**Answer: FV**
questions.shortcut: First letter −2, second letter −4 (wrap after A); H → F, Z → V.

questions.q:
Select the option that is related to the second letter cluster in the same way as the third letter cluster is related to the fourth letter cluster and fifth letter cluster is related to sixth letter cluster.

? : VI :: DB : BY :: ZC : XX
questions.solution:
In each pair the first letter moves 2 steps back (D → B, Z → X) and the second letter is replaced by its opposite letter, i.e. position $27 - n$: B(2) → Y(25), C(3) → X(24). Applying the same to XR: X(24) − 2 = V and the opposite of R(18) is $27 - 18 = 9 =$ I, giving VI ✓.

**Answer: XR**
questions.shortcut: First letter −2, second letter → its opposite (27 − position); XR → VI.

questions.q: If the month of September 2025 started on Wednesday, then which date will be the first Monday of March 2026?
questions.solution:
Days from 1 Sep 2025 to 1 Mar 2026 $= 30 + 31 + 30 + 31 + 31 + 28 = 181$. $181 \div 7$ leaves remainder 6, so 1 Mar 2026 = Wednesday + 6 = Tuesday. Hence the first Monday of March 2026 is 7 March.

**Answer: 7**
questions.shortcut: 181 days after Wednesday leaves remainder 6 → 1 Mar is Tuesday, so the first Monday is 7 Mar.

questions.q: The calendar for the year 1995 will be the same as which of the following years?
questions.solution:
Days from 1 Jan 1995 to 1 Jan 2006: 11 years containing the leap years 1996 and 2000, i.e. $365 \times 9 + 366 \times 2 = 4018$ days, and $4018 \div 7 = 574$ weeks exactly (0 odd days). Both 1995 and 2006 are ordinary (non-leap) years, so their calendars are identical. (2001 is too near: $2192$ days leave 1 odd day; 2007 and 2019 also fail.)

**Answer: 2006**
questions.shortcut: A non-leap year repeats after 11 years when the gap has exactly 2 leap years — 1995 + 11 = 2006.

questions.q: 5 persons A, B, C, D and E are sitting around a circular table facing towards the centre (not necessarily in the same order). Only one person is sitting between C and D, while considering towards right of D. B is sitting second to the left of D. A is sitting to the immediate right of B. Who is sitting second to the left of E?
questions.solution:
Facing the centre, take 'left' as the clockwise side. B is second to the left of D and A sits to the immediate right of B; C sits second to the right of D (exactly one person between). The only circle satisfying all clues is, clockwise: A → B → C → E → D. Second to the left of E: E → D (first) → A (second).

**Answer: A**
questions.shortcut: Clockwise order A-B-C-E-D fits every clue; two seats clockwise from E lands on A.

questions.q: 5 persons P, B, S, V and T are sitting in a row facing north (not necessarily in the same order). V and T are not immediate neighbours. There is only one person to the right of S. P and S are immediate neighbours. No one is sitting to the left of T. P is sitting next to B. Who is sitting at the right end of the row?
questions.solution:
Only one person is to the right of S, so S is 4th of 5; no one is to the left of T, so T is 1st. P is an immediate neighbour of S, so P is 3rd; P is next to B, so B is 2nd; V takes the remaining 5th seat (V and T are not neighbours ✓). Row: T, B, P, V, S — the right end is V.

**Answer: V**
questions.shortcut: Fix S at 4th and T at 1st first; the rest fall in place as T-B-P-V-S.

questions.q:
Two figures given on the left side of (::) are related with some logic/rule/relation. Select the missing figure on the right side of (::) from the given alternatives based on the same logic/rule/relation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9f9809dd336dfbb16d4a3fef2595dbce39f13e888f1759d8f94dd83764b3cc71.png]
questions.solution:
The number inside each figure equals its number of sides: the square (4 sides) contains 4. So the pentagon-shaped figure (5 sides) must contain 5, which only option A shows.

**Answer: Option A — pentagon with 5 inside**
questions.shortcut: Inside number = count of sides; pentagon → 5.

questions.q:
Two figures given on the left side of (::) are related with some logic/rule/relation. Select the missing figure on the right side of (::) from the given alternatives based on the same logic/rule/relation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/fd63d732b928b4ab299ebd236049be7b0df6b48d26a865c2d1f937b1ee8646ae.png]
questions.solution:
The inner arrow turns 90° clockwise at each step (down → left → up → right), so the missing figure has a right-pointing inner arrow. The outer corner arrow alternates NE–SW–NE–SW, so it must point to the bottom-left. Only option A shows a right arrow inside with the outer arrow at the bottom-left.

**Answer: Option A — inner arrow pointing right, outer arrow at bottom-left**
questions.shortcut: Inner arrow rotates 90° clockwise (next: right); outer diagonal alternates NE/SW (next: SW).

questions.q:
Arrange the given words in the sequence in which they occur in the dictionary.

1. Addition

2. Additive

3. Addictim

4. Addictive

5. Addict
questions.solution:
Compare letter by letter: 'Addic…' words come before 'Addit…' words. Among the c-words: Addict (shortest) < Addictim < Addictive (m < v). Among the t-words: Addition < Additive (o < v). Order: Addict(5), Addictim(3), Addictive(4), Addition(1), Additive(2) = 53412.

**Answer: 53412**
questions.shortcut: 'Addic…' before 'Addit…', shortest word first in its group → 53412.

questions.q:
Arrange the given words in the sequence in which they occur in the dictionary.

1. Adoption

2. Adoptive

3. Adopter

4. Adopting

5. Adopt
questions.solution:
Adopt is a prefix of all the others, so it comes first. Then compare the 7th letter onward: Adopter (e) < Adopting (g) < Adoption (o) < Adoptive (v). Order: Adopt(5), Adopter(3), Adopting(4), Adoption(1), Adoptive(2) = 53412.

**Answer: 53412**
questions.shortcut: Adopt first; then order by 7th letter e < g < o < v → 53412.

questions.q:
Select the option that is related to the second number in the same way as the third number is related to the fourth number and fifth number is related to sixth number.

(NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g.13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /subtracting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed)

 ? : 5694 :: 3645 : 3598 :: 2739 : 2692
questions.solution:
Each pair follows: first number − 47 = second number, since $3645 - 47 = 3598$ and $2739 - 47 = 2692$. Applying the same relation to the first pair: $? - 47 = 5694$, so $? = 5694 + 47 = 5741$.

**Answer: 5741**
questions.shortcut: Constant difference of 47 in every pair — add 47 to 5694.

questions.q:
Select the option that is related to the sixth number in the same way as the first number is related to the second number and third number is related to fourth number.

(NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g.13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /subtracting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed)

 4738 : 4771 :: 3927 : 3960 :: ? : 9025
questions.solution:
Each pair follows: second number = first number + 33, since $4771 - 4738 = 33$ and $3960 - 3927 = 33$. So $? + 33 = 9025$, giving $? = 9025 - 33 = 8992$.

**Answer: 8992**
questions.shortcut: Constant difference of 33 in every pair — subtract 33 from 9025.

questions.q: In a certain code language, 'denmark and supply theory' is coded as 'pm la sa tq' and 'theory come under economy' is coded as 'ls tq sn mq'. How will 'theory' be coded in that code language?
questions.solution:
'theory' is the only word common to both statements, and 'tq' is the only code common to both ('pm la sa tq' and 'ls tq sn mq'). Hence 'theory' is coded as 'tq'.

**Answer: tq**
questions.concept: Coding and Decoding in Fictitious Language
questions.shortcut: The word common to both sentences takes the code common to both.

questions.q:
A series is given with one term missing. Select the correct alternative from the given ones that will complete the series.

 {KEY50, HBV75, EYS112.5, ?, YSM253.125}
questions.solution:
Numbers increase 1.5 times each step: $50 \to 75 \to 112.5 \to 168.75 \to 253.125$ (check: $168.75 \times 1.5 = 253.125$ ✓). Letters move 3 places back each step (cyclically): KEY → HBV → EYS → BVP → YSM. Missing term = BVP168.75.

**Answer: BVP168.75**
questions.shortcut: Numbers ×1.5 and every letter −3 → BVP168.75.

questions.q:
A series is given with one term missing. Select the correct alternative from the given ones that will complete the series.

 {MPL100, NRO200, ?, PVU800, QXX1600}
questions.solution:
Numbers double each step: $100 \to 200 \to 400 \to 800 \to 1600$, so the missing number is 400. First letters advance +1 (M, N, O, P, Q), second letters +2 (P, R, T, V, X), third letters +3 (L, O, R, U, X). Missing term = OTR400.

**Answer: OTR400**
questions.shortcut: Numbers ×2; letters advance +1/+2/+3 position-wise → OTR400.
